payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. The independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit retracted the earlier 12,000-cycle claim, identifying an un-normalized depth-of-discharge error; the corrected cycle life is 8,400. Confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that point, requiring cycling to stop. The originating institution is Brennecke Institute.

The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle-life claim: the corrected cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, replacing the retracted 12,000-cycle figure. The confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. Projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that point, requiring cycling to stop.
